c.tagline: Limestone islands and warm Andaman tides.

avoid.reason: Jet-ski and motorbike rental-damage scams; drink-spiking in nightlife; high scooter-accident risk

hood_desc: The island's brashest beach resort town, famous for its long beach, packed nightlife and neon-lit Bangla Road. Ideal for party-seekers and first-timers wanting action and convenience.
A relaxed, family-friendly beach town with a broad sandy bay and a calmer vibe than nearby Patong. Best for couples and families wanting a laid-back beach holiday.
A scenic, upmarket beach area with a pretty bay, good sunsets and a moderate mix of dining and nightlife. Suits travelers wanting balance between relaxation and amenities.
The historic town center with colorful Sino-Portuguese shophouses, cafes, street art and markets. Great for culture seekers who prefer heritage charm over beaches.
A quieter, more low-key beach village popular with families and those seeking calm. Perfect for travelers wanting a peaceful, less crowded seaside stay.

The Memory at On On Hotel

water.note: Avoid tap water; stick to bottled or purified water to prevent stomach issues.

transit.pay: There's no citywide transit card - pay drivers directly in cash (Thai baht). Shared songthaews charge a flat 30-50 THB (~$0.85-1.40) around town; the newer Phuket Smart Bus (airport-Patong-Karon-Rawai) and Grab app rides can be paid by card in-app or cash.
transit.hours: Songthaews run roughly 6am-6pm (later on Patong's main routes); there is no scheduled night transit, so tuk-tuks, taxis, or Grab cover late-night trips.
transit.note: Most visitors get around by songthaew, metered taxi, tuk-tuk, rented scooter, or the Grab ride-hailing app - there is no rail or citywide bus network.

food.name: Mee Hokkien Phuket
food.desc: Phuket's own Hokkien noodles: fat yellow noodles wok-fried or braised in dark pork stock with prawns, fish balls and a fried egg on top.

places.name: Mee Ton Poe
places.note: Serving Hokkien noodles since 1946 near the clock tower; the island's benchmark bowl.

places.name: Ko Yoon
places.note: Tiny hole-in-the-wall widely rated by locals as the best Hokkien mee in town.

food.name: Moo hong
food.desc: Peranakan braised pork belly, slow-cooked in soy, garlic, white pepper and palm sugar until it collapses. The signature Phuket home dish.

places.name: Raya Restaurant
places.note: Grand old Sino-Portuguese house; the island's most famous address for Peranakan cooking.

places.name: Tu Kab Khao
places.note: Colourful Baba-Nyonya dining room doing moo hong and crab curry to a high standard.

food.name: O-tao
food.desc: A Phuket-only street griddle dish: oysters and grated taro fried into a sticky-crisp pancake with egg and bean sprouts.

places.name: Lock Tien Food Court
places.note: Phuket's oldest food court, relocated in 2025; the classic stop for o-tao and other Baba snacks.

places.name: Sunday Walking Street
places.note: Weekly night market where several griddles turn out o-tao under the shophouse arcades.

food.name: Kanom jeen Phuket
food.desc: Fermented rice noodles drowned in fish curry or coconut nam ya, eaten for breakfast with a tray of free herbs and pickles.

places.name: Pa Mai Kanom Jeen
places.note: Long-established Satun Road shop rated one of the island's best for kanom jeen.

places.name: Lock Tien Food Court
places.note: Kanom jeen counter alongside the dim sum and roti; go before 10am or it sells out.

food.name: Roti with curry
food.desc: Southern Thai-Muslim flatbread, flipped and griddled to order, torn and dipped into rich beef massaman or chicken curry.

places.name: Roti Thaew Nam
places.note: In the Michelin Guide every year since 2019; the beef curry is the reason to queue.

places.name: Roti Chaofa
places.note: Halal breakfast institution since the 1980s and a Michelin Bib Gourmand.

food.name: Phuket dim sum breakfast
food.desc: A Hokkien legacy: steamer baskets of pork dumplings, spare ribs and taro rolls eaten at 7am with tea, not as a lunch.

places.name: Boonrat Dim Sum
places.note: Early-morning local favourite; trolleys of steamers and gone by mid-morning.

places.name: Lock Tien Food Court
places.note: Heaving by 7am with dim sum, roti and kanom jeen counters side by side.

food.name: Kopitiam tea and oliang
food.desc: Old Chinese coffee-shop drinks: pulled milk tea and oliang, a bittersweet iced black coffee cut with cardamom and corn.

places.name: Kopitiam by Wilai
places.note: Vintage shophouse kopitiam; the tea and oliang are made the old Phuket way.

places.name: Roti Chaofa
places.note: Order tea to go with the roti, exactly as the morning regulars do.

food.name: Chalong Bay rum
food.desc: Phuket-made rum distilled from local sugarcane, drunk straight or in mojitos with Thai basil, lemongrass and kaffir lime.

places.name: Chalong Bay Rum Distillery
places.note: Tour the small distillery then take a cocktail class in the garden bar.

places.name: Ka Jok See
places.note: Cult Old Town bar-restaurant pouring Phuket rum cocktails into the small hours.

landmarks: Big Buddha Phuket
A gleaming 45-meter white marble Buddha statue crowning Nakkerd Hill, offering panoramic island views and one of Phuket's most recognizable landmarks.
Wat Chalong
Phuket's largest and most revered Buddhist temple, adorned with intricate golden chedis and murals, drawing worshippers and visitors alike to its ornate grand pagoda.
Promthep Cape
The island's dramatic southernmost headland is Phuket's premier sunset-viewing spot, where a lighthouse and rocky cliffs frame breathtaking views over the Andaman Sea.
Old Phuket Town
Colorful Sino-Portuguese shophouses lining historic streets like Thalang Road create a photogenic, museum-like district blending Chinese and colonial architectural heritage.
Patong Beach
Phuket's liveliest stretch of sand, lined with longtail boats, watersports, and a buzzing beachfront, epitomizing the island's vibrant tourist energy.
Karon Viewpoint (Three Beaches Viewpoint)
A hillside lookout revealing three sweeping crescent beaches at once, ranked among the finest panoramic vistas along Phuket's southwestern coastline.
Bangla Road
Patong's neon-lit nightlife strip bursts to life after dark with bars, street performers, and crowds, embodying Phuket's famously electric evening scene.
Kata Beach
A picturesque curved bay of soft sand and clear water, quieter than Patong yet equally scenic, popular for swimming, surfing, and sunset strolls.
Rang Hill (Khao Rang)
A wooded hill overlooking Phuket Town with a viewpoint, gardens, and open-air restaurants popular for sunset views over the old town's rooftops.
Naka Weekend Market
Phuket's largest weekend night market, a sprawling maze of stalls near Phuket Town selling street food, crafts, and secondhand goods.

train.note: Phuket has no railway at all. The nearest mainline station is Surat Thani, about 4-5 hours away by bus or minivan, with sleeper trains to Bangkok; book State Railway of Thailand tickets on the official D-Ticket site (https://www.dticket.railway.co.th), which has a partial English version.

bus.note: No direct international coaches run from Phuket - for Malaysia or Singapore you change in Hat Yai. The state operator Transport Co. Ltd (https://www.transport.co.th) and private companies run long-distance buses to Bangkok and southern Thailand from Phuket Bus Terminal 2.

ferry.note: There are no international ferries from Phuket. Local boats leave Rassada Pier year-round for Phi Phi, Krabi and Ao Nang, while Similan Islands trips are seasonal - the national park is closed roughly mid-May to mid-October.

half.name: Phi Phi Islands
half.blurb: People come for turquoise bays, towering limestone cliffs and the famous snorkeling at Maya Bay.

half.name: Phang Nga Bay & James Bond Island
half.blurb: Visitors sea-kayak among dramatic karst pinnacles rising straight out of emerald water.

half.name: Krabi & Railay Beach
half.blurb: Its soaring cliffs, hidden caves and world-class rock climbing draw beach lovers and adventurers.

half.name: Coral Island (Koh Hae)
half.blurb: A quick boat ride reaches calm white-sand beaches ideal for swimming and easy snorkeling.

half.name: Khai Islands
half.blurb: These tiny islets offer shallow clear water and colorful fish perfect for a relaxed beach day.

full.name: Similan Islands
full.blurb: Divers and snorkelers travel here for some of Thailand's clearest water and vivid coral reefs.
